name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q01 - Male reproductive structures, pollen wall, and viability

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements regarding the stamen, microsporangium, and pollen grains in angiosperms:

Statement I: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, dithecous, and tetrasporangiate.

Statement II: The outer three wall layers of a microsporangium protect and aid in anther dehiscence, while the innermost tapetum nourishes developing pollen grains.

Statement III: The hard outer exine of a pollen grain is composed of sporopollenin, which is absent at the germ pores.

Statement IV: In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 3-celled stage.

Statement V: Pollen grains of cereals such as rice and wheat lose viability within 30 minutes of their release.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In angiosperms, pollen grains develop within the microsporangia of the anther and exhibit specialised wall chemistry, cellularity at shedding, and species-dependent viability.

Step 2: Evaluation of Anther and Microsporangium Wall
A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with two thecae per lobe (dithecous) and contains four microsporangia at its corners (tetrasporangiate). Its outer three wall layers (epidermis, endothecium, and middle layers) provide protection and assist in anther dehiscence, while the innermost tapetum nourishes the developing pollen grains. Both descriptions are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Exine, Shedding Stage, and Viability
The pollen exine is made of highly resistant sporopollenin, which is absent at apertures called germ pores; this is accurate. However, in over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage (one vegetative cell and one generative cell), whereas only the remaining species shed at the 3-celled stage; thus, claiming over 60 per cent shed at the 3-celled stage is incorrect. Finally, rice and wheat pollen grains indeed lose viability within 30 minutes of release, which is accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Four of the five claims—covering the bilobed dithecous tetrasporangiate anther, microsporangium wall functions, sporopollenin exine with germ pores, and 30-minute viability in rice and wheat—are correct, while the claim regarding 3-celled shedding in over 60 per cent of angiosperms is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q02 - Pistil, ovule anatomy, megasporogenesis, and embryo sac

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the gynoecium, ovule, and female gametophyte:

Statement I: Papaver has a multicarpellary syncarpous pistil, whereas Michelia has a multicarpellary apocarpous gynoecium.

Statement II: The hilum represents the junction between the body of the ovule and the funicle.

Statement III: In a majority of flowering plants, all four megaspores produced by meiosis of the megaspore mother cell develop into functional embryo sacs.

Statement IV: The mitotic divisions of the functional megaspore nucleus up to the 8-nucleate stage are strictly free-nuclear.

Statement V: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate, with the filiform apparatus at the micropylar tip of the synergids.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Female reproductive development in angiosperms involves carpel organisation, ovule structure, meiotic megasporogenesis, and monosporic embryo sac formation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Gynoecium and Ovule Structure
Papaver bears fused carpels (multicarpellary syncarpous) while Michelia bears free carpels (multicarpellary apocarpous), and the hilum is the region where the ovule body fuses with its stalk (funicle). Both claims are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Megasporogenesis and Embryo Sac Development
In a majority of flowering plants, only one of the four megaspores remains functional while the other three degenerate, a pattern termed monosporic development; hence, claiming all four megaspores form embryo sacs is incorrect. The functional megaspore nucleus undergoes three strictly free-nuclear mitotic divisions to reach the 8-nucleate stage before cell walls are laid down, producing a 7-celled, 8-nucleate mature embryo sac where the synergids possess a micropylar filiform apparatus to guide the pollen tube. Both the free-nuclear division claim and the mature embryo sac organisation claim are accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Four claims—those describing Papaver and Michelia gynoecia, the hilum, free-nuclear mitotic divisions, and the 7-celled, 8-nucleate embryo sac with micropylar filiform apparatus—are correct, whereas the claim that all four megaspores become functional is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q03 - Pollination types, agents, and outbreeding devices

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following five statements regarding pollination and outbreeding devices in angiosperms:

Statement I: Cleistogamous flowers in Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina do not open and produce assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators.

Statement II: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, but genetically it is similar to autogamy.

Statement III: In Vallisneria, female flowers remain submerged and long, ribbon-like pollen grains are carried passively inside the water.

Statement IV: Monoecious plants such as castor and maize prevent both autogamy and geitonogamy.

Statement V: In Yucca, a moth species lays eggs in the ovarian locule and pollinates the flower, so neither species can complete its life cycle without the other.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Flowering plants use diverse pollination strategies and outbreeding devices that differ in their reliance on pollinators and their genetic outcomes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cleistogamy, Geitonogamy, and Yucca Mutualism
Cleistogamous flowers in Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina never open, making them invariably autogamous with assured seed-set even without pollinators. Geitonogamy transfers pollen between flowers of the same plant, so it is functionally cross-pollination but genetically equivalent to autogamy. In Yucca, the moth deposits eggs in the ovarian locule while pollinating the flower, forming an obligate mutualism. All three of these claims are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Hydrophily in Vallisneria and Monoecy
In Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the water surface on a long stalk and pollen is released onto the water surface; submerged female flowers with ribbon-like pollen carried inside water occur in marine seagrasses like Zostera, not Vallisneria. Furthermore, monoecious plants like castor and maize have separate male and female flowers on the same plant, which prevents autogamy but cannot prevent geitonogamy (unlike dioecious papaya, which prevents both). Thus, both the Vallisneria description and the claim that monoecy prevents geitonogamy are incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Exactly three of the five claims—those concerning cleistogamy, geitonogamy, and the Yucca–moth mutualism—are correct, while the claims regarding submerged pollination in Vallisneria and prevention of geitonogamy in monoecious plants are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q04 - Pollen-pistil interaction, hybridisation, and double fertilisation

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements regarding pollen-pistil interaction, artificial hybridisation, and double fertilisation:

Statement I: The pistil recognises compatible or incompatible pollen through a continuous dialogue mediated by chemical components of the pollen and the pistil.

Statement II: Emasculation is not required during artificial hybridisation if the female parent produces unisexual flowers.

Statement III: The pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle and discharges two male gametes into one of the synergids.

Statement IV: Syngamy produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus, whereas triple fusion produces a diploid zygote.

Statement V: Endosperm development precedes embryo development to provide assured nutrition to the developing embryo.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Compatible pollen recognition leads to pollen tube entry into the embryo sac and double fertilisation, while artificial hybridisation controls pollen identity using emasculation (only for bisexual flowers) and bagging.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pollen-Pistil Interaction and Artificial Hybridisation
Pollen recognition involves a chemical dialogue between pollen and pistil components, and emasculation is unnecessary when the female parent bears unisexual flowers (the buds are simply bagged before opening). After reaching the ovary, the pollen tube enters the ovule via the micropyle and releases two male gametes into a synergid. All three of these claims are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Double Fertilisation Products and Sequence
In double fertilisation, syngamy (fusion of one male gamete with the egg cell) produces a diploid zygote, whereas triple fusion (fusion of the other male gamete with two polar nuclei) produces a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). Reversing these products makes the fourth claim incorrect. Finally, endosperm development precedes embryo development to ensure assured nutrition for the embryo, which is accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Four of the five claims—covering chemical dialogue in pollen recognition, absence of emasculation in unisexual female flowers, micropylar pollen tube entry and gamete discharge, and endosperm preceding embryo development—are correct, whereas the claim reversing the products of syngamy and triple fusion is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER2_MCQ_Q05 - Post-fertilisation structures, seed longevity, apomixis, and polyembryony

questiontext.text:
Consider the following six statements regarding post-fertilisation events, apomixis, and polyembryony:

Statement I: Coconut water from tender coconut is free-nuclear endosperm, while the surrounding white kernel is cellular endosperm.

Statement II: In grass embryos, the single lateral cotyledon is called the scutellum, and the radicle and root cap are enclosed in an undifferentiated sheath called the coleorrhiza.

Statement III: Remnants of persistent nucellus in seeds such as black pepper and beet are referred to as perisperm.

Statement IV: Apple, strawberry, and cashew are examples of true fruits because they develop solely from the ovary.

Statement V: Excavated seeds of Lupinus arcticus germinated after an estimated 10,000 years of dormancy, and a 2,000-year-old viable seed of Phoenix dactylifera was discovered near the Dead Sea.

Statement VI: Converting hybrid crop varieties into apomicts prevents segregation of characters in the hybrid progeny, enabling farmers to reuse hybrid seeds year after year.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Post-fertilisation events encompass endosperm cellularisation, embryo differentiation, seed and fruit maturation, and specialised asexual seed mechanisms such as apomixis and polyembryony.

Step 2: Evaluation of Endosperm, Grass Embryo, and Perisperm
In tender coconut, coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm and the white kernel is cellular endosperm. In grasses, the lateral cotyledon is the scutellum and the coleorrhiza encloses the radicle and root cap. Black pepper and beet seeds retain persistent nucellus known as perisperm. All three descriptions are accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Fruit Types, Seed Longevity, and Apomixis
Apple, strawberry, and cashew are false fruits because the thalamus contributes to fruit formation alongside the ovary; calling them true fruits formed solely from the ovary is incorrect. The dormancy records of 10,000 years for Lupinus arcticus and 2,000 years for Phoenix dactylifera are accurate, and making hybrids apomictic prevents character segregation in progeny so farmers can reuse hybrid seeds annually, which is also accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Exactly five of the six claims—those regarding coconut endosperm, grass scutellum and coleorrhiza, perisperm, seed longevity records, and apomixis in hybrid crops—are correct, whereas the claim classifying apple, strawberry, and cashew as true fruits is incorrect.
